questions.prompt: What does next/image do automatically? Select all that apply.

options.text: Serves appropriately sized images in modern formats
Reserves space to prevent layout shift
Removes the need for an alt attribute

questions.explanation: next/image optimizes size/format, lazy-loads, and reserves space. It still requires a meaningful alt for accessibility.

questions.prompt: For a remote (URL) image with next/image, what must you provide that a local import supplies automatically?

options.text: Nothing — remote images need no extra info

questions.explanation: Next.js can't read a remote image's intrinsic size, so you pass width and height (or use fill) and allow the domain in images.remotePatterns.

questions.prompt: Which module self-hosts fonts at build time with no layout shift? Type the import path (e.g. next/x...).
questions.explanation: next/font (e.g. next/font/google) downloads and self-hosts fonts at build time and reserves space to avoid layout shift.

questions.prompt: A file at public/brochure.pdf is served at which URL?
questions.explanation: Files in public/ are served as-is from the site root, so public/brochure.pdf is available at /brochure.pdf.

questions.prompt: Match each need to the right tool.
questions.explanation: next/image optimizes images, next/font handles fonts, public/ serves static files, and a static export needs unoptimized images (no server to optimize at runtime).

questions.prompt: Order the steps to display an optimized local image.

items.text: Import the image file (e.g. import hero from './hero.jpg')
Next.js reserves space, then lazy-loads and optimizes it

questions.explanation: A local import gives Next.js the dimensions; <Image> then reserves space (no layout shift) and optimizes and lazy-loads the image.
